visual.general_description: Fourteen rows of paired line plots of daily QIDS-SR depression scores, one row per participant, for the pre-treatment and post-treatment periods.
visual.detailed_description: A tall figure with two columns headed Pre-Treatment and Post-Treatment and fourteen rows labelled Participant 1 to Participant 14 on the left. Each cell is a small line plot with a black line joining black points, a purple dotted series and a grey band with a dashed outline around the purple series. Every plot has x axis tick labels 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25, and the word Days is printed under the bottom plot of each column. A long black arrow runs up the left side beside the rotated title Depression (QIDS) Score, and a long black arrow runs horizontally under the bottom of the figure. Each row has its own y axis tick labels, for example 0, 10 and 20 in some pre-treatment plots and 0, 2, 4 and 6 in some post-treatment plots. No legend, numeric data labels or statistics are printed on the plots.

evidence.quote: QIDS-SR, Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology
QIDS-SR, Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology

pixel_observations: Two columns headed Pre-Treatment and Post-Treatment and fourteen rows labelled Participant 1 to Participant 14 are printed.
Each plot has a black line with black points, a purple dotted series and a grey band with a dashed outline.
The black line is broken in several plots, for example Participant 3, 5, 9 and 11 in the pre-treatment column and Participant 2 in the post-treatment column, where consecutive days are not joined.
Y axis tick labels differ from row to row and between the two columns; x axis tick labels are 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 in every plot.
The title Depression (QIDS) Score is printed rotated beside a vertical arrow and the word Days is printed under the bottom plot of each column.
No numeric values are printed on the plots.

caption_claims.value: QIDS-SR daily mood scores for 28 days pre-treatment and 28 days post-treatment per participant

evidence.quote: The QIDS-SR daily mood scores for 28 days pre-treatment (left hand side) and 28 days post-treatment (right hand side), per participant.

caption_claims.value: Black points and line show the QIDS-SR score and purple points the best model fit

evidence.quote: Individual mood plots show the QIDS-SR score (black points and black line), best model fit from time-series analysis (purple points).

caption_claims.value: Predicted values from the overall time-series model are shown with an approximate 95% CI band in grey

evidence.quote: Predicted values (from the overall time-series model pre- and post-treatment) are shown with an approximate 95% CI band in grey.

caption_claims.value: Participants are presented in order of starting mood monitoring

evidence.quote: Participants presented in order of starting mood monitoring.

clinical_significance.statement: Per the article text, patients had complex correlated mood scores before treatment, described by a threshold autoregressive model, and simpler, less variable mood dynamics after treatment, described by an autoregressive model.

evidence.quote: Clinically, before treatment, patients had complex correlated mood scores (described statistically with a threshold autoregressive TAR(2) model). After treatment, patients had simpler, less variable mood dynamics (described by autoregressive (AR(2)) model).

limitations: Participant labels are printed on the image only and are not linked to case descriptions in the text; no individual patient is identified.
Participant row labels are not used as panel labels; the figure is described as one whole panel.
No values are read from plot geometry; only printed text and qualitative shape are recorded.

assignments.subject: aggregate

evidence.quote: The QIDS-SR daily mood scores for 28 days pre-treatment (left hand side) and 28 days post-treatment (right hand side), per participant.

assignments.rationale: The caption describes daily QIDS-SR plots per participant of the 14-participant series; the participant labels exist only on the image and the source gives no individual identity evidence, so the figure is not attributed to a roster patient.

limitations: The article has no individual patient roster; Participant 1 to Participant 14 are image labels only.
Pixels of the full figure were viewed, including zoomed halves; the 28 small plots were described only qualitatively.

visual.general_description: Fourteen per-participant Markov chain diagrams with coloured circles at the corners of pre-treatment and post-treatment triangles.
visual.detailed_description: Fourteen small diagrams are arranged in a grid of four columns, with Participant 1 to Participant 14 printed above them (the last row holds two diagrams). Each diagram is a slanted frame of thin lines joining two triangles drawn with thick black outlines; the lower triangle is labelled Pre-Treatment and the upper triangle is labelled Post-Treatment, each label split over two lines. Coloured filled circles of red, orange and green sit at the corners of each triangle, and their sizes differ between participants and between states. No numbers, axes, tick labels or colour legend are printed on the image.

panels.general_description: Fourteen small diagrams, one per participant, each showing coloured circles of different sizes at the corners of two triangles labelled pre-treatment and post-treatment.
panels.detailed_description: Fourteen small diagrams are arranged in a grid of four columns, with Participant 1 to Participant 14 printed above them (the last row holds two diagrams). Each diagram is a slanted frame of thin lines joining two triangles drawn with thick black outlines; the lower triangle is labelled Pre-Treatment and the upper triangle is labelled Post-Treatment, each label split over two lines. Coloured filled circles of red, orange and green sit at the corners of each triangle, and their sizes differ between participants and between states. No numbers, axes, tick labels or colour legend are printed on the image.
pixel_observations: Fourteen small diagrams, each titled Participant 1 to Participant 14, in a grid of four columns.
Each diagram has two triangles drawn with thick black outlines joined by thin lines; the lower one is labelled Pre-Treatment and the upper one Post-Treatment.
Filled circles in red, orange and green appear at the triangle corners, with circle sizes that vary between participants and states; very small circles appear as dots.
No printed numbers, axes or colour legend are present on the image; the colour meaning appears only in the caption.

evidence.quote: Markov chain analysis of changes in QIDS-SR daily scores for individual participants pre- and post-treatment.

evidence.quote: Circle size represents the probability of a patient being in a certain mood state

caption_claims.value: Red circles represent moderate levels of depression, orange circles mild levels and green circles absence of depressive symptoms

evidence.quote: red circles represent moderate levels of depression (QIDS-SR⩾9); orange circles represent mild levels of depression (QIDS-SR⩽9 and not equal to 0); green circles represent the absence of any depressive symptoms (QIDS-SR=0)

caption_claims.value: The front triangle shows the 28-day baseline phase and the back triangle the 28-day post-treatment phase

evidence.quote: this gives a picture of transition between states during their 28-day baseline phase (front triangle) which can be compared with their 28-day post-treatment phase (back triangle)

clinical_significance.statement: Per the article text, in 11 of 14 cases there was an improvement in mood profiles, with a decreased occurrence of high QIDS-SR scores after treatment.

evidence.quote: This analysis showed that in 11 of 14 cases, there was an improvement in mood profiles with a decreased occurrence of high QIDS-SR scores

limitations: Circle sizes are not converted into probabilities; no values are printed.
The caption threshold wording for mild and moderate states overlaps at the value 9; kept as printed in the caption.
Participant labels are printed on the image only and are not linked to case descriptions in the text.
No probability values are read from circle sizes; only printed text and qualitative appearance are recorded.
